{'empty_input': False, 'translation': 'Earlier this month, Google launched the all-new Pixel 11 series. Compared with the previous-generation Pixel 10, the overall changes in the new device are not that significant, but it has added some delightful user experience optimisations. One of them is a brand-new camera processing option, allowing you to have more detailed control over the final look of the entire photo.'}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': 'On the eve of the iPhone 18 Pro launch, I hope Apple will also introduce a similar feature.'}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': "Pixel 11 has added a new camera feature called Camera Looks, which is to a certain extent similar to the iPhone's Photographic Styles, allowing you to adjust the way the camera processes shots. These adjustments are made before the photo is taken, and are far more than just a simple filter."}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': "Google offers quite a few preset styles, similar to Apple's approach, and you can also fine-tune the effect of each preset. Besides these common options, there are several styles that capture new trends in mobile photography: Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie and Minimal."}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': 'These styles deliberately steer clear of the over-processed look of current smartphone photos, attempting to recapture the flavour of old-school photography. As the name suggests, Digi is meant to deliver the narrow dynamic range, high contrast and noise-filled look of those compact, pocket-sized cameras from the 2010s.'}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': 'As for Minimal, it goes to the opposite extreme, minimising computational processing as much as possible. Many HDR pipelines will not kick in, letting you see what the smartphone sensor truly captures. You can head over to 9to5Google to check out the relevant sample photos.'}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': "Using the iPhone's ProRAW format, you can in theory restore the photo to a state that does not look overly post-processed, but doing so somewhat defeats the purpose of shooting with a phone."}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': 'Conclusion'}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': "If Apple wants to become the best camera in everyone's pocket, it needs to understand that not every user wants the same kind of result. Photographic Styles is a good start, but Apple should go further. When all is said and done, photography is an art form of self-expression, so giving users a few more options to control the degree of computational processing on their photos is the right direction. Apple should take a leaf out of Google's book and add a 'Minimal' style to the iPhone."}

{'empty_input': False, 'translation': "What are your thoughts on the current state of iPhone photography? Do you like Apple's recent Photographic Styles changes, or do you think there's still room for improvement? Feel free to leave a comment and share your views."}
